rulings.reason: The instruction scores how an achievement is phrased -- vivid, plain-language, easily-visualized milestone versus abstract numeric delta -- so two abstracts reporting the identical result would diverge purely on rhetorical framing, which is a writing-style channel rather than evidence about the research. It is mixed because genuinely landmark results are more naturally describable as memorable milestones, so the upstream cause can also produce real quality.

Reporting exact margins, error values, and specific quantitative detail is a property of the underlying empirical evidence and its verifiability, not a surface fingerprint: it exposes claims to checking and is standard evidence-reporting craft, which Track A explicitly covers. The 'not whether results are good' clause shifts it from magnitude to rigor of reporting, which remains substantive rather than incidental.
